title: Admission Horizon Estimator and Microfusion Scheduler to Reduce Tail Latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We are still seeing 95th/99th token latency spikes on mixed short/long request workloads even after recent batch-shaping work. Analysis shows many spikes come from mismatches between the batch admission window and downstream kernel suitability (e.g., attention kernel choices that prefer larger homogeneous batches). Additionally, prefill requests that suddenly transition into long decodes cause latent kernel reconfiguration and KV-cache churn, worsening tail latency.

Proposal: Implement an Admission Horizon Estimator (AHE) combined with a Microfusion Scheduler (MFS).
- AHE: a lightweight per-request estimator that predicts the expected remaining token horizon (short/medium/long) using features available at request time (prompt length, input tokens, user-provided max_tokens, model family, and recent tenant-level distribution). This runs in the admission path and tags requests with an "admission-horizon" hint.
- MFS: a short-timescale scheduling layer that groups incoming requests into microwindows (~5-25ms) that prioritize homogeneous horizon groups while preserving per-request latency SLOs. Microfusion uses admission-horizon hints plus kernel affinity heuristics to select target kernels and when to emit a prefill batch vs. hold for a tiny window to improve kernel fit.

Goals: reduce 95/99 token-latency across mixed workloads by minimizing kernel reconfiguration and KV cache thrash; improve decode stability for prefill->decode transitions; keep average latency and throughput stable or improved.

Design details:
- Feature set for AHE: prompt_length, truncated_input_fraction, user_max_tokens, model_variant_tag, tenant_historical_pct_long (sliding window), request_priority. A simple logistic regression with calibrated thresholds serves initial estimator (fast, <1ms). We will evaluate moving to a tiny neural model if accuracy is insufficient.
- Microwindows: tunable microwindow_size_ms (default 12ms), max_hold_tokens budget per microwindow, and priority lanes (latency-sensitive vs. throughput). The MFS will attempt to coalesce same-horizon requests up to batch size thresholds determined by the kernel selector. If a microwindow completes without suitable coalesced batch, requests are forwarded to a fallback fast path to avoid SLO violations.
- Kernel affinity: extend kernel selection metadata to include preferred horizon and batch shape ranges. MFS queries kernel profiler to pick kernel variant (e.g., int8-gemm attention kernel vs. fused-attention) that maximizes throughput for the expected batch shape.
- KV-cache handling: add a micro-prefetch marker in the prefill phase so kernel selection can reserve cache slots and avoid eviction during immediate decodes.

Metrics and success criteria:
- 95th token latency reduced by >=20% on mixed short/long synthetic workload (existing benchmark harness).
- 99th token latency reduced by >=15% without >=3% regression in median latency or throughput.
- No customer-visible increase in error-rate or memory OOMs.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged canary in canary-region with low traffic (runtime-1.26 canary).
2) Observability: new dashboards: admission-horizon distribution, microwindow occupancy, kernel-affinity match rate, KV cache churn per tenant.
3) Gradual ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on SLO violations.

- Kernel affinity spec: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/kernel-affinity-spec

acceptance_criteria: AHE inference latency < 1.5ms p95 under normal admission path load
Microfusion coalescing increases kernel-homogeneous batch fraction by >=30% on mixed workloads
95th token latency down >=20% on synthetic mixed workloads
No memory OOM or error rate regression observed during 50% traffic ramp in canary region
implementation_steps: Prototype AHE (logistic regression) in admission path; add unit and perf tests
Extend kernel metadata to include horizon preferences and batch-shape ranges
Implement Microfusion Scheduler with microwindowing and fallback fast-path
Integrate KV-prefetch marker into prefill protocol and kernel interface
Add metrics (horizon histogram, microwindow occupancy, kernel match rate, kv churn), dashboards and alerts
Run synthetic benchmarks and iterate thresholds; prepare rollout playbook
risks: Estimator misclassification causing increased latency for latency-sensitive requests (mitigation: confidence threshold to force fast-path)
Microwindowing could add headroom latency if misconfigured (mitigation: strict per-request max-hold and rapid fallback)
Kernel preference metadata mismatch could reduce throughput (mitigation: A/B kernel selection in bench harness)
KV-prefetch logic could increase cache pressure if too aggressive (mitigation: tenant-level cache quotas and conservative prefetch)
Feature-flag complexity and rollout coordination across runtime, kernel repo, and observability
dependencies_notes: Depends on kernel-affinity metadata work (ENG-31247) and microwindowing primitives (ENG-271828). Requires the KV cache reservation API landed in ENG-543210 or a short-lived shim. Coordination with infra for canary rollout and with benchmarks team for synthetic scenarios.
